plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because your payment only depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win). Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you if you win against a bid between your value and your bid. Underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $22.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and the price you pay never depends on your own bid except in determining whether you win. Overbidding risks paying more than your value; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this holds regardless of what others do, I will bid exactly my value of $34.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do—since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid), overbidding risks losing money if you win, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my value of $10, regardless of beliefs about opponents' strategies.
